CANONICAL_NAME.value: WalkSAT -- Kautz and Selman (stochastic local search for SAT)

VERSION.value: Kautz's Walksat repository default branch as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: GSAT (1992) -> WalkSAT (1994, Selman, Kautz, Cohen): STOCHASTIC LOCAL SEARCH for SAT -- flip the variable that minimises broken clauses, with a random-walk escape; an incomplete solver that finds models fast but never proves UNSAT. The opposite paradigm to CDCL (MiniSat/PicoSAT).

value.built_to: find a satisfying assignment for a hard SAT instance quickly by hill-climbing on the count of unsatisfied clauses with random restarts and walks
value.pressure: instances where systematic search is too slow but a model exists; the trade of completeness for speed
value.success_means: an assignment satisfying all clauses within a flip budget; it cannot report UNSAT

ANCESTRY.value: GSAT (1992) -> WalkSAT (1994, Selman, Kautz, Cohen): STOCHASTIC LOCAL SEARCH for SAT -- flip the variable that minimises broken clauses, with a random-walk escape; an incomplete solver that finds models fast but never proves UNSAT. The opposite paradigm to CDCL (MiniSat/PicoSAT).

cut.note: stochastic local search for SAT as three mechanisms: pick an unsatisfied clause at random and flip one of its variables; choose the variable by a heuristic over two incrementally maintained counts per variable (how many clauses a flip would break, how many it would make), with a noise probability of a random choice; and keep the counts exact after every flip by touching only the clauses containing the flipped variable. Novelty adds a tie-break on the variable's age so the search does not undo its last move

organs.human_name: flipatom (463-610): breakcount[] and makecount[] (166-167); for each clause of the flipped literal: a clause going true or false, or changing its number of true literals, adjusts the counts of the variables involved; the freebie list of variables with breakcount 0 and makecount > 0
organs.mechanism: each clause knows how many of its literals are true and which one is the sole true literal when that number is one; flipping a variable walks its occurrence lists: a clause that becomes false increments the makecount of all its variables and removes the flipped one from breakcounts; a clause that goes from one true literal to two releases the break responsibility of the previously critical variable; a clause that goes from two to one makes the remaining true variable critical (its breakcount rises); variables with zero break and positive make are kept on a 'freebie' list because flipping them is always an improvement
organs.output: updated counts and the unsatisfied-clause list
organs.state: numtruelit per clause, breakcount, makecount, the false-clause list, the freebie list
assumptions: a variable's effect on the clause count is a local function of the clauses it occurs in; maintaining it incrementally makes a flip O(occurrences) rather than O(clauses)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: millions of flips per second; the reason local search became competitive on random and structured instances
organs.human_prior: GSAT's score maintenance (Selman, Levesque, Mitchell 1992); the break/make split is WalkSAT's

organs.human_name: pickbest (1666-1691): tofix = false[random]; bestvalue = min breakcount over the clause; if (nofreebie || bestvalue > 0) and random < p then a random variable of the clause, else a random best
organs.mechanism: an unsatisfied clause is chosen uniformly; among its variables the ones with the smallest breakcount are collected; if some variable breaks nothing it is taken (a free move), otherwise with probability p (the noise) a uniformly random variable of the clause is flipped and with 1 - p one of the best; the clause is thereby satisfied at every step and the damage elsewhere is minimised or randomised
organs.input: the false-clause list and the counts
assumptions: always satisfying the chosen clause focuses the walk; break count alone (not net gain) is the right score; noise is needed to escape local minima and the free-move exception costs nothing
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the SKC rule (Selman, Kautz, Cohen 1994) that made WalkSAT beat GSAT and complete solvers on hard random 3-SAT
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the optimal noise p depends on the instance (the reason the adaptive option exists); it cannot prove unsatisfiability

organs.human_name: picknovelty (1918-1965): diff = makecount - breakcount; best and second best with age (changed[var]) as tie-break; youngest; 'if best != youngest return best; else with probability p second_best'; plus_flag (Novelty+: a 1 percent random walk) vs numflip % 100
organs.mechanism: in the chosen unsatisfied clause, variables are scored by net gain (make minus break), ties broken toward the older variable; if the best variable is not the one flipped most recently in the clause it is taken; if it is, the second best is taken with probability p; independently a random variable is taken every hundredth flip (or with probability 1 percent in the Novelty+ variant), which is what makes the walk provably able to leave any region
organs.input: the counts and the flip ages
organs.state: changed[] (the last flip time per variable)
assumptions: flipping the variable just flipped back is the dominant failure of greedy walks; an age tie-break plus a probabilistic refusal is cheaper than a tabu list
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: Novelty (McAllester, Selman, Kautz 1997) and Novelty+ (Hoos 1999) outperform SKC on structured instances
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: without the periodic random walk Novelty can loop (Hoos's finding, which the plus variant fixes)

organs.human_name: -adaptive PHI THETA (214-218, 723-734): last_adaptive_objective, adaptive_phi 0.2, adaptive_theta 0.2; the update sites not read
organs.mechanism: starting at zero noise, the search watches the number of unsatisfied clauses; if it has not improved for a while (theta times the clause count) the noise is raised by phi of the remaining range, and on an improvement it is lowered faster; so the walk is greedy while progress is made and random when stuck
assumptions: the best static noise is instance-dependent and unknowable in advance; the objective's stagnation is a usable signal
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: removes the noise parameter from the user's hands (Hoos 2002)

pressures.source_evidence: walksat.c flipatom, pickbest, picknovelty, the adaptive option
pressures.condition: an organism searches assignments of a satisfiable CNF by flipping variables; the score is time to a model over a suite of random and structured instances; unsatisfiable instances may be present (the organism cannot prove them, only time out)
pressures.resource_or_constraint: flips per second; a noise setting
pressures.failure_condition: cycling between the same assignments, or flips that cost O(clauses) each
pressures.world_punishes: pure greedy (GSAT without noise); recomputing scores from scratch; flipping back the last move
pressures.world_rewards: incremental counts, clause-focused random walk with noise, age-aware refusal, adaptive noise
pressures.observable_consequence: median flips to a model on uf250 random 3-SAT and on a structured family, for GSAT, SKC at fixed p, Novelty+ and adaptive noise; the fraction of runs that cycle without the periodic random walk
pressures.vacuity_condition: 2-SAT or instances solved by unit propagation
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a complete solver on small instances (the world uses instances where CDCL is slower)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given a model must verify it in one pass; GSAT with zero noise must get stuck on the structured family where SKC succeeds; Novelty without the periodic walk must show cycling that Novelty+ removes: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: incomplete SAT solving by local search (Selman, Kautz, Cohen 1994; Kautz's distribution 2004-)
